function_question: How does nature move crowds without jams?

opening.text: There was a boy called Omid who loved playing football with his friends at break time.
When the bell rang, the whole school squeezed down one hallway towards one door to the playground.
The crowd got so stuck that break was nearly over before Omid got outside. "Why does this happen EVERY day?" he groaned.

card.place: The school hallway at break time
card.goal: Redesign how people move so the jam disappears
card.rules: No boss allowed, just simple rules for everyone

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Every break, Omid's school gets stuck in a giant hallway jam. Can you help him redesign how people move, so the jam disappears? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some designers already have a spark of an idea for moving big crowds. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been moving huge crowds for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four heroes who never get stuck!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which door design will get 10 marbles through fastest?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your hallway from above, like a bird looking down!
guide.build_and_test: Build your model hallway and time 20 counters. How fast can your crowd get through the door?
guide.retry_tip: Designers never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing, like the lanes or the door, and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Omid's school follows YOUR simple rules, and everyone gets out to play in seconds.

quick_check.question: With Omid's new lanes, 2 children pass through the door every second. How many seconds does it take for 20 children?
quick_check.right: Right! 20 ÷ 2 = 10 seconds. A smooth-flowing door is much faster than a jammed one.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. How many groups of 2 are there in 20?

clue_cards.name: Army ants
clue_cards.trick: Ants heading out use the sides, ants coming home use the middle.
clue_cards.does: With no head-on crashes, the trail keeps flowing.

clue_cards.name: Fish school
clue_cards.trick: Each fish keeps a small gap and matches its neighbours' speed.

clue_cards.name: Starlings
clue_cards.trick: Each bird copies its 7 or so nearest neighbours.
clue_cards.does: Thousands of birds swirl together like one cloud.

clue_cards.name: Honeybees
clue_cards.trick: A busy hive can have more than one doorway.
clue_cards.does: The bees spread out between the doors so traffic keeps moving.

items.label: Everyone rushes to the door at once
Two lanes: keep left going out, keep left coming in
Friends stop right in the doorway to chat

predict.explain: Jams start when streams of people crash into each other or stop in a narrow spot. Lanes and steady speed keep everyone moving.

lab.title: The marble door lab
lab.predict: Tilt the tray and let 10 marbles run to the door. Which design gets them through fastest?
options: A small post before the door

tool.name: How Might We
tool.intro: You already know all 4 parts: User, Need, Insight and How might we. Today you'll put them together into one strong question, all by yourself.

parts.name: User
parts.starter: The people stuck in the hallway are…

parts.name: Need
parts.what: What do they need to do? Use an action word.
parts.example: 🍱 He needs to open his lunchbox by himself.

parts.name: Insight
parts.what: What did you notice that surprised you?
parts.example: 🍱 His fingers are too small to pull the tight lid.
parts.starter: I noticed the jam starts when…

parts.name: How might we…?
parts.what: Join them into a hopeful question to design for.
parts.example: 🍱 How might we make a lid small hands can pop open?
parts.starter: How might we help… so that…?
